--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.network_smooth()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Smooth node scores over the network topology. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.network_smooth()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Smooth node scores over the network topology. title: >- [Graph.network_smooth()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Smooth node scores over the network topology. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Smooth node scores over the network topology. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47663-L47833){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.network_smooth( scores, alpha=0.5, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Smooth node scores over the network](../assets/graphs/network-smooth.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: the shared seven-node graph with raw scores as badges, 1 on A, B and D and 0 elsewhere, the scored nodes outlined. After: the smoothed scores, shaded as heat. C, a 0 surrounded by scored neighbors, rises to 0.45, while the far triangle E, F, G stays near 0." width="100%"} Propagates noisy per-node scores (e.g., differential expression values) through the network to produce denoised estimates that incorporate neighborhood information. Uses iterative label spreading: `f(t+1) = alpha * W_norm * f(t) + (1 - alpha) * f(0)`. At each iteration every node receives a share of each neighbor's current score: a neighbor passes its score on divided by its degree (or, in weighted graphs, scaled by the edge weight divided by its total edge weight). The node's new score blends that neighborhood sum with its own original score, using `alpha=` as the mixing weight. Iteration stops when no score changes by more than `tol=` or after `max_iter=` rounds. The result keeps each node anchored to its measured value while pulling it toward its neighbors, so an isolated high score is damped and a node with a low score but strongly scored neighbors is raised. This is useful for: - denoising per-gene statistics (fold changes, -log10 p-values) using an interaction network - spreading a signal from a few scored nodes to unscored nodes nearby - preparing scores for module detection, as in `gwas_pipeline()` In directed graphs scores flow along edge direction, from source to target, so a node only receives signal from its predecessors. Because each node splits its score among its neighbors, smoothed values are generally smaller than the raw ones; compare them relative to each other rather than to the original scale. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [scores]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[Union[int, str], float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping nodes, as integer IDs or string labels, to initial scores. Nodes not in the dictionary default to `0.0`. Integer keys that are not in the graph are ignored, and an unknown label raises an error. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing strength between `0` and `1`. The default is `0.5`. Higher values give more weight to network neighbors and spread the signal further; lower values preserve the original signal, and `alpha=0` returns the input scores unchanged. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of smoothing iterations. The default is `100`, which is ample for most graphs with `alpha=` well below `1`; higher `alpha=` values converge more slowly. A small value such as `1` performs just that many propagation steps, which limits how far the signal travels. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance. Iteration stops once the largest absolute change in any node's score between two iterations is below this value. The default is `1e-6`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute the smoothed scores are stored under when `return_dict=False`. If `None` (default), the attribute is named `"network_smooth"`. Overwrites an existing attribute of the same name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the smoothed scores as a dictionary (`attr_name=` is then ignored). If `False` (the default), store the scores as a node attribute (see `attr_name=`), record the computation so it is listed by `describe()`, and return `self` for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph | dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Smoothed scores (if `return_dict=True`) or `self`. The dictionary has an entry for every node in the graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `alpha=` is outside `[0, 1]`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~random_walk_with_restart`) : Score nodes by a walk that keeps returning to the seeds. [](`~heat_diffusion`) : Spread a signal from the seeds by diffusion. [](`~gwas_pipeline`) : Smooth scores, find modules and rank them in one call. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A score of `1.0` at one end of a path leaks along it, fading with each step from `A`. A higher `alpha=` trusts the neighbors more, so `A` keeps less and the far end gets more: ::: {#49a7db6e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ( path.network_smooth({"A": 1.0}) .network_smooth({"A": 1.0}, alpha=0.8, attr_name="alpha_08") .get_node_df() .select("label", "network_smooth", "alpha_08") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

REP3 barely changed though all four of its partners went up, and ENZ3 went up more than any protein but REP5 though none of its partners did. Smoothing pulls each measurement toward its partners': ::: {#33b8318d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl proteins = ec.proteins() proteins.network_smooth(proteins.get_node_attrs("expression"), attr_name="smoothed") ( proteins.get_node_df() .filter(pl.col("label").is_in(["REP3", "ENZ3"])) .select("label", "expression", "smoothed") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Ranked by smoothed change, ENZ3 now comes after six proteins of the disease module around REP1: ::: {#9b70b6f6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( proteins.get_node_df() .sort("smoothed", descending=True) .select("label", "pathway", "expression", "smoothed") .head(8) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
